title: Adding thin strips to find the area under y = x²
examples: How do thin rectangles give the area under a curve?
What is the area under y = x squared from 0 to 1?

items.label: Exact area: 1/3
items.ask: Why is the exact area one third?

explain.say: How would you measure the area under a curved line? Here is a trick: cover it with thin rectangles and add them up. We want the area under y equals x squared, from 0 to 1. Look at the first bar: with 4 strips the total is about 0.219.

draw.text: Adding thin strips to find the area under y = x²

items.label: Exact area: 1/3
items.ask: Why is the exact area one third?

explain.say: Each strip is a rectangle: width times height, and the height comes from the curve. But the strips sit under the curve and miss little bits on top. So 0.219 is too small. Do you think more strips will help?

items.label: Exact area: 1/3
items.ask: Why is the exact area one third?

explain.say: Yes! Look at the next bar: 10 thinner strips give 0.285. The gaps on top shrink. Now 100 strips, the third bar, give 0.328. See the bars creeping up?

items.label: Exact area: 1/3
items.ask: Why is the exact area one third?

explain.say: As the strips get thinner and thinner, the total gets as close as you like to one number: one third, the last bar. That exact answer is the integral of x squared from 0 to 1.

items.label: Exact area: 1/3
items.ask: Why is the exact area one third?

explain.say: Well done! Adding up endless thin strips is integration. Archimedes used a trick like this over 2000 years ago to find the area under a parabola. Today computers add millions of strips in a blink.

items.label: Exact area: 1/3
items.ask: Why is the exact area one third?

faq.a: A Riemann sum adds up the areas of thin rectangles under a curve to estimate the area. With more and thinner rectangles, it gets closer to the exact area.
Here each strip takes its height from its left edge, where the rising curve is lowest, so the top of each strip sits under the curve and misses a small piece.
asks: Why is the estimate too small?

faq.q: Why is the exact area one third?
faq.a: The integral of x squared is x cubed over 3. From 0 to 1 that gives 1 over 3 minus 0, which is one third.
asks: How do you integrate x squared from 0 to 1?

faq.q: Does using more strips always help?
faq.a: Yes, for a smooth curve the error shrinks as the strips get thinner. In the limit of infinitely many strips you get the exact area.
asks: What happens with infinitely many strips?

faq.q: What does the integral sign mean?
faq.a: The tall S shape stands for sum. Leibniz chose it because an integral is a sum of infinitely many thin strips.
asks: Why is the integral sign an S?

facts: The integral of x² from 0 to 1 equals 1/3.
With 10 left-hand rectangles, the estimate of the area under y = x² from 0 to 1 is 0.285.
